q: Can a Chilean exporter deduct Chile's green tax from CBAM?
title: Chile's green tax and CBAM
short: Only for CBAM goods, and only for tax actually paid on the emissions behind them, with proof and independent certification. Chile's tax, about US$5 per tonne on large emitters, mostly hits power and mining, and copper is not a CBAM good, so few exports qualify.
audience: Chilean producers of steel, cement or fertilisers selling to the EU

p: Large stationary sources above the law's thresholds pay per tonne of CO2. Check the current rate and thresholds.

ul: Tax paid on the installation's emissions, per tonne of goods exported.
Not offsets used to reduce the bill.

p: Copper cathode is outside CBAM, so there is nothing to deduct from. Copper buyers ask for footprints for their own reporting instead.

senseible: Senseible keeps each site's fuel, power and production records together, so the embedded emissions you send an EU importer trace back to dated documents.
